Variants.Content: Royal peace refers to the ideal that the monarch should protect roads, markets, messengers, and subjects from unprovoked violence. It never happens automatically and must be maintained by guards, courts, and predictable punishments; the people often judge the king by whether they can get to the next town safely.

Entry The King's Peace Royal peace refers to the ideal that the monarch should protect roads, markets, messengers, and subjects from unprovoked violence. It never happens automatically and must be maintained by guards, courts, and predictable punishments; the people often judge the king by whether they can get to the next town safely. They start by asking who is obligated, who is protected, and who will seek justice after a breach of contract.
